title: Quote to Contract Automation: A Complete Guide (2026)
summary: Quote to contract automation streamlines the transition from sales proposals to signed legal documents by eliminating manual data entry tasks.
body_markdown:
## Building the quote to contract workflow in Activepieces


Activepieces synchronizes document generation with CRM status changes across 748+ integrations without embedding proprietary logic into the sales platform.


By offloading the contract assembly to an external workflow, teams prevent the data silos that occur when legal templates are locked inside a single CRM.


Activepieces publishes its core under an MIT license, ensuring the logic governing these contract flows remains a company asset rather than a rented service. Open the LICENSE file in the activepieces/activepieces repository to see the MIT terms on the core, with enterprise directories kept under a separate commercial license for advanced governance. This structure allows teams to build complex legal automations without the risk of a vendor paywalling the very logic their revenue depends on.


### Setting up the deal stage updated trigger


The workflow initiates when the HubSpot "Deal Stage Updated" trigger detects a status change to "Contract Requested." This ensures the automation only fires after a salesperson has performed the necessary manual validation.


Activepieces processes these deal properties (including the primary contact’s email and the total contract value) using an MIT-licensed core that can be self-hosted to keep sensitive legal data on your own infrastructure. Without this specific trigger, the document generation would require a manual export of data, which introduces the risk of human transcription errors.


### Step 2: Using the 'generate document' action


The CRM data maps to the DocuSign "Create Envelope from Template" action to populate the legal agreement with the correct pricing and terms. This step ensures that the legal language remains consistent across all deals.


The signing platform manages the template rather than a text field in the CRM. The screenshot of a payment notification workflow demonstrates this principle: a Stripe "Payment Failed" trigger connects directly to a Slack "Send Message To A Channel" action, providing immediate visibility into transaction status.


This visibility allows the finance team to intervene before a service interruption occurs. The subsequent step in a contract flow would then wait for the signature status to update before proceeding.


Activepieces enables this progression through Git Sync and Release Management, allowing teams to promote flows from a test environment to production as versioned code. Check the Activepieces documentation for Release Management to see how it separates projects and environments to make promotion a deliberate step. Organizations like MoneyGram and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production to maintain this level of control over their critical business logic.


### Step 3: Branching for high-value contract approvals


A "Branch" step evaluates the total contract value from the initial deal data to determine if the document requires a secondary internal signature. The system routes contracts exceeding a specific internal threshold to an "Approval" action.


This action pauses the flow until a manager grants permission via an email button. This gate prevents unauthorized discounts from being sent to clients, a control that is often absent in basic point-to-point integrations.


### Step 4: Automating the final PDF archival


Once the "Envelope Signed" webhook is received from DocuSign, the final executed PDF is uploaded to a Google Drive folder via the "Upload File" action to meet long-term audit requirements.


This centralizes all signed instruments in a secure repository that is independent of the sales team's daily environment.
